title: Vegetable Scrap Broth: The $0 Ingredient
editorialNotes: No PantryPal occurrence (Tier 1 CTA is anonymous); no swap.
$6-10 store-value figure is body copy, not hero type.

thread.element: freezer bag filling with scraps across weeks
thread.endState: full bag beside a jar of broth

copy.headline: Every time you chop vegetables, you throw away free broth.
The system: keep a gallon-size freezer bag in your freezer.
items: Every time you cook, toss vegetable scraps into the bag.
When the bag is full — usually 2–3 weeks — you make broth.

copy.headline: Save these:
items: Onion skins and ends. Carrot peels and tops. Celery leaves and ends. Mushroom stems.
Herb stems (parsley, thyme, cilantro). Garlic skins. Corn cobs. Leek tops.

copy.headline: Skip these:
items: Brassicas (broccoli, cabbage, cauliflower) make broth bitter.
Potato peels make it starchy and cloudy.
Anything moldy or rotten — freezing doesn't fix that.

copy.headline: Full bag + water + salt + 45 minutes simmering.
copy.body: Strain. That's 8 cups of broth worth $6–10 at the store. Made from scraps you were going to throw away.

copy.headline: The best ingredient in your kitchen costs nothing. It's already in your trash can.
